correctness.rationale: Exact all-n proof: strict diagonal dominance and tridiagonal Green factorization; monotone positive left/right factors; Tonelli yields strictly positive interval coefficients for squared mixtures including cross shifts; interval count balancing proves all-budget optimality and uniqueness; spectral integral representations cover log and fractional inverse; polynomial localization and Fourier series prove homogeneous log variance density. Exact-rational verifier passed 21587 assertions; direct matrix-log numerical verifier passed 21184 comparisons. Experiments are not the infinite proof.

evidence: Trace-variance objective is a weighted within-color pair sum, equivalently a maximum k-cut for weights |(log A)_{ij}|^2. This weight family is stricter than arbitrary Robinson/Monge similarities: every strict upper-triangular squared entry is an *upper interval sum* of strictly positive coefficients.
The interval-square proof reduces all partition comparisons to balancing each interval simultaneously; the general graph-color literature searched did not exhibit this exact log-matrix statement.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A general max-k-cut formulation is not an implication of its minimizer: graph weights matter. The constructed mixed-resolvent interval positivity establishes the needed special structure. A published stronger theorem for all positive interval-decomposable kernels would imply the claim, but none was found in the inspected or indexed sources.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary full-text sections and indexed semantic records were compared at the level of objectives and theorem implications. Earlier inverse-resolvent path variance results cover the single point-mass subfamily, but not the square of an integrated resolvent matrix (log determinant), for which cross terms need the new positive interval-square certificate. value.rationale: Stochastic estimation of log determinants and fractional inverse traces is a well-motivated numerical problem. Exact class-supported probing variance has a fully classified robust optimizer across every heterogeneous weighted path and probe budget. The nonnegative gap certificate quantifies alternatives; the homogeneous limit gives a concrete explicit performance law. The cross-resolvent square theorem is not a mere substitution of the already-known single-resolvent path case; neither the Chebyshev estimator nor distance-color minimum-number theorems imply it. The exact-action and independence restrictions are explicit.
